questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must drive carefully where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. Impaired driving endangers you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden weather change means you should change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It impairs your thinking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time and reduces your coordination and balance. Alcohol also hurts your vision and your ability to judge distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when you drive.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady green light, let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first. You can continue driving, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to avoid crashes.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and keep drivers safe. They tell you about road conditions and help guide you. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect driving abilities.
Help keep drivers alert.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a crash, stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: They are weaving between lanes.
They are driving slower than normal traffic.
They are making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than normal traffic, jerking movements, and making quick sudden stops.

questions.question: It is an infraction to smoke a cigarette:

options.text: If a child is in the vehicle.
While driving in a residential area.
If you are driving at night.
While driving between May and September.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a child is in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot smoke in a vehicle if a child age 15 or younger is present. This is an infraction.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Get back at the other driver by cutting them off.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before changing lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move left or right.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions per mile, so you must focus on driving. Any extra task can be dangerous.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, a driver should slow down, look, and listen.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing without warning devices, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Alcohol combined with other drugs can increase the effects of both. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Continue to the next exit, then safely turn around and go back.

questions.question: Only vehicles with disability plates or placards may park in spaces marked for people with disabilities.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Parking spaces for people with disabilities can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road may become wet and slippery.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do if a police officer stops you?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel and stay in your vehicle. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Only get out if the officer asks you to. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance cards.
